instruments.evidence: Phase 4a-1: a price setting for a call minute, a call_minute usage kind, and the billing service pricing it and checking the first minute is affordable. The kind leaves the backend in the usage response and in every ledger row a call will write, so the review followed it to the credits panel.

No ledger covers billing or usage kinds. The TranslationKeysExist test's own comments record the same failure once before: 'chat' had no label and the usage list read omnichat.commerce.usage.chat down the page.

Printed the setting for four inputs through the config test: empty 3, '5' 5, '0' 3, 'three' 3. Printed the usage-cost map: call_minute 3 by default, 5 after SetCallMinuteCost(5), still 5 after SetCallMinuteCost(0).

Read the labels the credits panel renders from en.json: chat Message, voice 'Voice call', image, video, other -- and no call_minute. The voice kind is charged in omnichat_voice.go:149-155, the speak button reading one message aloud, so beside real call minutes it would read as a second kind of call. Finding R2.
The usage endpoint returns {usage, costs: UsageCosts(), limit}; costs now carries call_minute. Its one frontend reader takes costs.image, so the extra key is inert.
usage_kind is VARCHAR(64); the ledger's CHECK only requires it on debits, so call_minute needs no migration.
The backend now writes call_minute; the TypeScript union stopped at video, and en.json had no label, so the panel builds omnichat.commerce.usage.call_minute and renders the key itself. Finding R1.
OmniChatCreditUsageItem.usage_kind is typed by the union the panel reads; OmniChatBillingCosts names only voice, image and video, and nothing reads the others.
Two lists of usage kinds -- the Go constants and the TypeScript union -- and the guard compared the union with its labels, never with the Go list, so a kind added in Go alone passed it. Finding R3.

instruments.why: No external provider or worker contract.

instruments.evidence: CallCreditsPerMinute is read in Load and asserted through Load; the cost map is written in the constructor and the setter and read by UsageCosts, ReserveOwned and the affordability check.
The affordability check is tested through a wallet fake that answers the real GetWallet read, on both balances.
The new guard reads the real backend source file, not a copied list.
A configured price is used; enough credits across both balances pass.
Zero, negative and non-numeric prices fall back to 3 in config and are ignored by the setter; a subscriber is not included.
Exactly the price in credits is affordable; one short is not.
The video affordability check and the call-minute one now share one function.
Included special-cases image and video and returns false for them before the plan lookup; call_minute reaches the plan lookup and still returns false, which the subscriber test asserts.
Admins pass the affordability check and ReserveOwned bypasses them, as for video.
The default price is one named constant.

After R1 and R2, searched for every other place that spells the usage kinds or promises calls: no backend switch over kinds misses call_minute; the platform UpgradeModal's 'Voice calling' is the user-to-user messaging plan, not OmniChat; OmniChatUpgradeModal mentions no calls.
All three controlled; see findings.
The label guard is reachable -- it runs in the frontend suite -- and was blind to the backend; it now reads the Go constants itself.
